data.title: NYC delivery bill: Amazon warns shoppers of higher prices; Mamdani says it's greed
data.description:
Amazon (AMZN) is appealing to shoppers to oppose New York City's proposed legislation that would require the e-commerce giant to obtain a city license and directly employ its delivery workers.

"NYC Council could add up to $5 per order," a popup warning flashed when New Yorkers opened Amazon's app or its website on Thursday.

Amazon (AMZN) warned that if the Delivery Protection Act, or Intro 518, passes, it'd be forced to consider moving operations out of the city. This would likely mean slower and costlier delivery for New Yorkers.

​​"As the City Council continues to review this bill, we want to be transparent with our customers about what it would cost them if it passes as written — which is why we're doing this," an Amazon (AMZN) spokesperson said regarding the popup alerts.

The company urged its customers in New York City to contact their City Council member and ask them to oppose this bill.

The warning on Amazon's (AMZN) platform also linked to a form that automatically drafts a message to council members, where customers just need to fill their names and addresses.

"This bill could increase my annual delivery costs by up to $664 per year," the message read. "In a city already facing an affordability crisis, that's money I cannot afford to lose — and neither can my neighbors."

Within the first six hours of launching this campaign, New York City customers sent around 20,000 emails to council members opposing the legislation, The Wall Street Journal reported.

In response, New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani doubled down on his support for the legislation. 

"Amazon is a multi-trillion dollar company," he posted on X. "If Jeff Bezos adds $5 to your order, it's not because of City Council's efforts to protect workers' rights and keep our streets safe. It's greed."

"We are crafting legislation that regulates Amazon and protects workers, without impacting prices or jobs," New York City Council Speaker Julie Menin said. "If Amazon thinks this deceptive campaign will effectively threaten New Yorkers and intimidate this City Council, they are dead wrong."

data.title: Anthropic to join MSCI Large Cap, FTSE Global indexes after Nasdaq debut
data.description:
Anthropic (ANT) has been added to key FTSE Global Equity Index Series benchmarks through a fast-entry process, effective Dec. 21, FTSE Russell said Thursday.

The additions cover the FTSE All-World Index, FTSE MPF All-World Index, FTSE Developed Index, FTSE Global Large Cap Index, and FTSE Developed ex Multinational Index.

The Claude developer will also join the large-cap segment of the MSCI Global Standard Indexes after the close of trading on Nov. 30, MSCI said.

The decision follows confirmation that the company’s full and free-float-adjusted market capitalizations, based on its Thursday’s closing price, meet MSCI’s early-inclusion criteria.

Anthropic made its Nasdaq debut on Thursday, opening at $111.50, a 34.3% premium to its $83 offering price, and closing at $97.17.

data.title: IT Tech Packaging receives going concern warning
data.description:
• IT Tech Packaging (ITP) independent auditor issued a going concern warning, citing substantial doubt about the company's ability to continue operations.
  • The warning follows a $24.3M net loss and $5.4M in operating cash outflows for FY2025. The auditor highlighted these conditions in the company's annual report filed November 19.
  • Management cited cost optimization, manufacturing capacity adjustments, director financial support and access to a $150M credit facility as measures to address the uncertainty.

data.title: Asia tech stocks reel from Anthropic IPO as SoftBank, Samsung, and TSMC slide
data.description:
• Shares of Japan’s SoftBank Group (SFTBY) tumbled 16.16% on Friday, amid a broader decline in Asian technology stocks following the much-anticipated stock market debut of Anthropic (ANT). 
  • SoftBank, one of the biggest backers of OpenAI (OPENAI), Anthropic’s rival, with a total investment of  $64.6B in the ChatGPT maker, suffered the worst day in over two years.
  • Additionally, the company's ownership of chip designer Arm (ARM) has made its shares particularly sensitive to shifts in sentiment toward the AI sector. The stock lost 30% in October and is down 31% so far this month.
  • Japanese semiconductor stocks also tumbled, with Tokyo Electron (TOELF) dropping 7.06%, Lasertec (LSRCY) down 9.21%, and Renesas Electronics (RNECF) losing 7.02%.
  • The sell-off extended to South Korea, where Nvidia (NVDA) suppliers SK Hynix (SKHY) and Samsung Electronics (SSNLF) fell 5.92% and 7.01%, respectively, pressuring the benchmark Kospi, which ended 5.21% lower.
  • Meanwhile in Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co., or TSMC (TSM), closed 4.76% lower in Taiwan. Elsewhere, Chinese tech giant Tencent (TCEHY) fell 2.01%, while memory chipmaker CXMT slid 5.31% to a record low. Baidu (BIDU) declined 4.79%, while AI chipmaker Enflame, regarded as one of China’s “four little dragons,” dropped 7.16%.

data.title: KBR prices $500M of 7.25% senior notes for planned Trinzic spin-off
data.description:
• KBR (KBR) said that its wholly owned subsidiary, Solar MTS Holdings LLC, has priced a private offering of $500M in aggregate principal amount of 7.25% senior notes due 2035.
  • The offering is expected to close on or about December 4, 2026.
  • The notes are being issued in connection with KBR's planned spin-off of its Mission Technology Solutions (MTS) business into an independent, publicly traded company, Trinzic Inc. The separation is expected to be completed on January 4, 2027.
  • Proceeds, alongside term loans Trinzic expects to draw at the spin-off, will fund a cash distribution to KBR and related expenses. KBR plans to use the distribution to repay debt.
  • The proceeds will remain in escrow pending completion of the spin-off. If conditions are not met by March 31, 2027, the notes will be redeemed at par plus accrued interest. Upon completion, Trinzic will assume the notes, guaranteed by its domestic subsidiaries.

data.title: UK retail sales increase 2.3% Y/Y in October, topping estimates
data.description:
• The UK’s retail sales volumes increased 0.7% M/M in October 2026, beating economists’ expectations for no growth, according to data released by the Office for National Statistics. The increase followed a 0.4% decline in September.
  • On a Y/Y basis, retail sales volumes rose 2.3%, accelerating from 0.8% growth in the previous month and exceeding consensus estimates of 1.7%.
  • The stronger-than-expected reading points to an improvement in consumer spending, with both monthly and annual retail sales growth exceeding market forecasts.

data.title: Frontline Non-GAAP EPS of $2.38 beats by $0.12, revenue of $921.26M beats by $203.84M
data.description:
• Frontline press release (FRO): Q3 Non-GAAP EPS of $2.38 beats by $0.12.
  • Revenue of $921.26M (+112.9% Y/Y) beats by $203.84M.
  • Declared a cash dividend of $2.38 per share for the third quarter of 2026.
  • Achieved average daily spot time charter equivalent earnings ("TCEs")2 for VLCCs, Suezmax tankers and LR2/Aframax tankers in the third quarter of 2026 of $148,500, $102,500 and $67,800 per day, respectively.
  • Sold two VLCCs built in 2017 for a total sales price of $270.0 million. The transactions generated net cash proceeds of $179.0 million.
  • Entered into a three-year time charter-out agreement for one Suezmax tanker, built in 2016, at a rate of $80,000 per day, which commenced in October 2026.
  • Outlook: "We expect the spot TCEs for the full fourth quarter of 2026 to be lower than the spot TCEs currently contracted, due to the impact of ballast days during the fourth quarter of 2026. We expect the Suezmax time charter TCE for the full fourth quarter of 2026 to be higher due to the profit share for the remaining period."

data.title: Gaming and Leisure Properties prices $600M senior notes offering at 6.25%
data.description:
• Gaming and Leisure Properties (GLPI) priced a public offering of $600M of 6.25% senior notes due December 15, 2031.
  • The notes, which will be issued by its operating partnership, GLP Capital, L.P., and its wholly owned subsidiary, GLP Financing II, Inc., were priced at 99.486% of their principal amount and carry a coupon of 6.25%. The notes will represent senior unsecured obligations of the issuers and will be guaranteed by Gaming and Leisure Properties.
  • Net proceeds will be used for working capital and general corporate purposes, which may include funding existing and new development commitments, acquisitions, development and expansion projects at existing and new properties, repayment of indebtedness, capital expenditures and other business purposes.
  • The offering is expected to close on December 1, 2026.
